title: Tiganopsomo
description: Tiganopsomo is a traditional Greek fried bread, crisp and golden on the outside with a soft, warm center. Often filled with salty feta cheese, it balances rich, savory flavor with a simple homemade dough.
story: In a small mountain village in Greece, the smell of warm dough and sizzling olive oil drifted through the narrow stone streets every Sunday morning.
Yiayia Eleni always woke before the sun. She would tie her apron, dust the wooden table with flour, and begin making tiganopsomo for the family table.
details: Use warm water, not hot water, so the yeast can work gently.
Seal the feta inside the dough well so it melts without leaking into the pan.
Fry over medium heat so the outside turns golden while the inside cooks through.
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and olive oil, then knead until the dough is soft and elastic.
Cover and let the dough rise for about 1 hour.
Flatten each piece, add feta in the center, seal it closed, and press gently into a flat round.
Fry over medium heat in a little oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with honey or oregano.
